maya: heads-up — offline replay run against last-night's trace flagged a weird kernel-selection churn when sequence lengths spike. p50 ok, but p99 jumped ~18% for the 2:00–2:15 window. attaching short log excerpt.

maya: ```
replay: trace=prod-latency-2026-03-17.bin
config: batch_policy=continuous, token_budget_target=96, queue_policy=fifo_coalesce
kernel_log: select_kernel(model=v2-ll, seq=192) -> kernelA
kernel_log: select_kernel(model=v2-ll, seq=16) -> kernelB
kernel_switches: 1342 in 15m
p99_latency: 128ms -> 152ms
```

sam: hmm, kernel switches that frequently sound like sequence-length fragmentation in the batch. did the replay pack variable-length requests without prefix padding? :thinking:

maya: replay uses trace-preserved seq lengths (we replay requests as-is to measure realistic behavior). note that the high-switch period aligns with a traffic burst of lots of short queries mixed with a few long chat sequences.

leon: suggestion: try token_budget_target=64 and increase coalesce window (max_coalesce_ms) to allow more short requests to aggregate into stable kernel shapes. also consider prefilling KV cache for long sequences so they don't break batch shape mid-step.

ash: (not in thread)

ashley: quick note on KV warming — when a long request lands in a batch with many short requests, KV cache gets touched at different offsets and triggers extra memcpy/evict ops. in replay we can simulate prefetch by replay flag `--kv-warmup=on` to see impact.

sam: can you share the exact replay command you used? i'll run an A/B with the proposed params.

maya: sure — baseline command:

maya: ```bash
./replay-run --trace=prod-latency-2026-03-17.bin \
  --model=v2-ll --policy=continuous --token-budget=96 \
  --queue=fifo_coalesce --duration=15m --preserve-seqlen
```

maya: proposed A/B change (candidate):

maya: ```bash
./replay-run --trace=prod-latency-2026-03-17.bin \
  --model=v2-ll --policy=continuous --token-budget=64 \
  --queue=fifo_coalesce --max_coalesce_ms=8 \
  --kv-warmup=on --duration=15m --preserve-seqlen
```

perf-bot: perf-summary (baseline vs candidate small-run 20k reqs): baseline p99=152ms, candidate p99=129ms (:thumbsup: 15% improvement). cost per token w/ batching up ~1.8% (expected due to increased coalesce latency). full-run queued.

leon: nice. baseline p50 unaffected? we care mostly about p99 tail for SLAs.

perf-bot: baseline p50=34ms, candidate p50=36ms (small bump), p95 baseline=72ms candidate=68ms.

sam: ok will run full A/B next hour for 1M replayed requests. question: does the A/B harness record kernel-selection histograms? i'd like to verify reduced kernel churn.

maya: yes — add `--collect=kernel_hist,kernel_switches,kv_evictions` to the command. those metrics are shipped to the replay DB.

ashley: couple pitfalls to watch: 1) increasing max_coalesce_ms helps short queries but can worsen tail for interactive flows if client-side latency budgets are tight; 2) kv-warmup increases memory pressure on GPUs if many thumbs are warmed simultaneously. keep an eye on OOM counters.

sam: running now. i'll post results in this thread. expected finish ~20m.

perf-bot: regression-alert suppressed for this candidate run. baseline alert still active for last-night burst window.

maya: after 1M replayed requests (A vs B): candidate reduces kernel_switches by 62% in the 2:00–2:15 window, p99 improved 14% end-to-end. but observed a small cluster of OOM warnings on one machine during overlapping warmups — tracked to node gpu-12.

leon: action items:
- add node-level stagger for kv-warmup (random jitter on start) to avoid hotspot warmup.
- keep token_budget_target=64 for this workload class (chat+mixed short requests), but expose as per-route override.
- run longer soak (6h) to ensure no regressions in edge windows.

ashley: filed infra ticket to add jittered warmup: INFRA-4821. assigned to infra-eng.

sam: i'll open an internal PR with the A/B harness config and kernel_hist plots attached.

maya: tl;dr: offline replay A/B shows that lowering token_budget_target and enabling KV warmup + slightly larger coalesce window cuts kernel churn and improves p99, at small p50 cost and manageable memory tradeoffs. next: roll candidate to canary fleet with per-route override and 6h soak.

leon: :thumbsup: ship the canary, monitor kernel_switches and gpu-ooms closely.
